audits.mathematicalReason: Extend BA beyond A to T with AT = AC = x. Since M bisects arc CAB, arcs CAM and MB are equal, so MC = MB. The inscribed-angle theorem gives ∠MAC + ∠MAB = 180°, hence ∠MAC = ∠MAT. Triangles MAC and MAT are congruent by SAS, giving MT = MC = MB. Thus triangle TMB is isosceles, and its altitude MP bisects TB. Consequently PB = TP = TA + AP = x + (x + 1) = 2x + 1. This validates the proposed synthetic route without making it the only possible method.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let consecutive polygon interior angles be α_i. In the illustrated exterior-tip configuration, the triangle on each intervening side has tip angle θ_i = α_i + α_(i+1) - 180°. Summing gives S = 2·180(n - 2) - 180n = 180(n - 4). Equivalently, exterior turns e_i give θ_i = 180° - e_i - e_(i+1), with total exterior turn 360°. However, convexity and nonparallelism do not ensure e_i + e_(i+1) < 180°. For the triangle formed by the three supporting lines, the general unsigned angle is |180° - e_i - e_(i+1)|. A convex pentagon with interior angles 60°, 60°, 140°, 140°, 140° satisfies the specified nonparallelism, but these unsigned angles total 300°, not 180°. The candidate's scope routes are defensible for the intended configuration, and its stated limitations must be retained.
limitations: The intended formula requires every adjacent pair of polygon interior angles to sum to more than 180°, or an equivalent condition ensuring the illustrated exterior-tip configuration.

audits.derivedAnswer: C: PQ is always equal to the length of an external common tangent.
audits.mathematicalReason: Let U and V be the internal-tangent contact points, both between P and Q. Equal tangent lengths show that the external common tangent through P has contact-to-contact length PU + PV, while the one through Q has length QU + QV. Reflection in OO' makes these two external lengths equal, say L. Adding gives 2L = (PU + QU) + (PV + QV) = 2PQ, so L = PQ. The auxiliary-circle route is also valid: tangent-angle bisectors imply ∠OPO' = ∠OQO' = 90°, placing P and Q on the circle with diameter OO'. If the original radii are R and r and OO' = d, its center has distance |R - r|/2 from PQ, giving PQ = √(d² - (R - r)²), exactly the external common-tangent length.

figureEvidence.fact: The circles are externally separate. P and Q are the intersections of the displayed internal tangent with the two external tangents. Both internal contact points lie between P and Q, and each of P and Q lies between the two contact points on its corresponding external tangent.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let U and V be the centers of semicircles SAR and RBT. Arc degree measure gives ∠AUR = a and ∠RVB = b. Taking the rightward baseline as direction 0°, the radii UA and VB have directions a and 180° - b. Perpendicularity of tangent and radius then gives the pictured rays PA and PB directions 90° + a and 90° - b. Their convex included angle is therefore a + b, with no factor of one-half. Tangent perpendicularity is directly assessed, while angle addition is supporting work.
